comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Lending risk-adjusted margin and purchase volumes
comparisons.peer_summary: Total risk-adjusted margin decreased 85 bps driven by higher net credit losses, while total credit card and debit card purchase volumes increased to $368.9 billion and $557.0 billion respectively, reflecting higher consumer spending.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC reported increased credit costs in their consumer/card portfolios in 2024, driven by similar factors including vintage maturation and macroeconomic pressures, though BAC also highlighted increased consumer spending volumes alongside its margin compression. C attributed its higher cost of credit primarily to a 45% rise in net credit losses from maturing card vintages and macroeconomic pressures on lower FICO customers. BAC reported a decrease in its total risk-adjusted margin driven by higher net credit losses, while simultaneously noting an increase in total credit card purchase volumes, reflecting higher consumer spending levels.

sentences.text: Cost of credit increased to $8.6 billion, compared to $6.7 billion in the prior year.

The increase was driven by higher net credit losses (up 45%), primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years, as well as macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment impacting both cards portfolios, with lower FICO band customers primarily driving the increase.
Total risk-adjusted margin decreased 85 bps primarily driven by higher net credit losses, partially offset by higher net interest margin and higher net fee income.
Total credit card purchase volumes increased $5.7 billion to $368.9 billion, and debit card purchase volumes increased $29.9 billion to $557.0 billion, reflecting higher levels of consumer spending.
